The decreasing values of resistivity with increasing aging temperature correlate with the observed changes in microstructure. As more solute and interstitial are removed from solid solution into precipitates, the resistivity of bcc solid solution alloys decreases.
The decrease in hardness correlates with the precipitation of solute and interstitial elements along grain boundaries, resulting in a softening of the matrix.
the grain boundary precipitates appear to be responsible for tensile embrittlement of the alloy following aging at 1398 K

Taken together, the microstructure, resistivity and hardness data suggest that aging for 1100 h causes progressively enhanced precipitation of Hf-rich precipitates ... The formation of the grain boundary precipitates reduces the matrix interstitial solute content and thereby causes overall softening of the matrix.
The 1098 K aged specimen exhibited DSA for elongations greater than 7–8%.

conflicts.description: Higher aging temperature led to increased nitrogen impurity, which could cause embrittlement, but the authors state it does not fully explain the degradation, and no impurity pickup was measured at 1098 or 1248 K.

evidence.quote: N content in the samples following aging at 1398 K may have some influence on the mechanical behavior of the specimens. However, it does not fully explain the extent of degradation of T-111 after aging.
